name: The Lesser Court of the Hawk and Hare
description: A small, traveling court of the Aelaerem and Aelinnel that settles disputes too petty for the great courts and too important for simple blood-price. They speak for the land and the Hollow in equal measure, and their verdicts are neither cruel nor kind—they are exact. They ask no money, only a story that is true and a promise that is kept. Their symbol is a hawk and a hare, held in balance.
location: The Valewood edge, Theona, and the Eastern Dolmis
leverage: Neutral arbitration, temporary sanctuary, red-thread wards, and a network of hedge-walkers who will relay messages without betrayal.
debtTrigger: When Obligation fills, the Court calls in its price: a single, irrevocable judgment. You will adjudicate a dispute between two parties who cannot be reconciled—and your ruling will be binding on all.
quirk: The Court's rulings are given not in words, but in a piece of red thread tied in a specific pattern. The patterns are never repeated; each knot is a unique memory.
keyNPCs: The Hallower (an old woman who has walked nine thousand miles and whose voice is so soft it is often mistaken for the wind)
The Keeper (a silent Aelinnel who tends the Court's pile of memory-ropes)
The Witness (a young Theona hedge-witch who can read the truth in a way that makes everyone uncomfortable)
hooks: A dispute over a buried ancestor—two families claim the same barrow. The Court has asked for an outside arbiter who does not know the history.
A member of the Court has broken its own code. The Hallower is weeping. She needs someone to find the Keeper before the Hollow does.
An angry Vhasian knight has sworn to burn the Court's grove unless it rules against his rival. The Hallower has asked for a story that can make him laugh—or weep—instead.
